configuration.notes: Use this fixture to verify that verbose open-ended questions stay verbose and explanation-oriented after generation.

questions.source_raw: During a week-long field test for an autonomous hospital delivery cart, engineers notice that the cart enters the final straight section of the corridor at \(4.8\,\text{m/s}\) while a constant braking system can provide only \(1.6\,\text{m/s}^2\) of deceleration. The cart is \(6.5\,\text{m}\) from a sealed lab door, and the faculty supervisor wants a written justification rather than a single numerical answer. Explain whether the cart stops before it reaches the door, and show how the relevant kinematics relationship supports your conclusion.
questions.stem: During a week-long field test for an autonomous hospital delivery cart, engineers notice that the cart enters the final straight section of the corridor at \(4.8\,\text{m/s}\) while a constant braking system can provide only \(1.6\,\text{m/s}^2\) of deceleration. The cart is \(6.5\,\text{m}\) from a sealed lab door, and the faculty supervisor wants a written justification rather than a single numerical answer. Explain whether the cart stops before it reaches the door, and show how the relevant kinematics relationship supports your conclusion.
questions.answer: Using \(v_f^2 = v_i^2 + 2a\Delta x\) with \(v_f=0\), \(v_i=4.8\,\text{m/s}\), and \(a=-1.6\,\text{m/s}^2\), the stopping distance is \(\Delta x = 7.2\,\text{m}\). Because \(7.2\,\text{m} > 6.5\,\text{m}\), the cart would still be moving when it reaches the door. The braking system alone is therefore insufficient to stop the cart in time.

questions.source_raw: A biomedical sensor package is launched straight upward from the roof of a clinic with an initial speed of \(18\,\text{m/s}\). Ignore air resistance unless a part states otherwise. (a) Determine the time it takes the package to reach its maximum height. (b) Which statement best describes the package's acceleration while it is in flight?
questions.stem: A biomedical sensor package is launched straight upward from the roof of a clinic with an initial speed of \(18\,\text{m/s}\). Ignore air resistance unless a part states otherwise.

parts.stem: Determine the time it takes the package to reach its maximum height.
parts.answer: At the highest point the vertical velocity is zero, so \(0 = v_0 - gt\). Using \(v_0 = 18\,\text{m/s}\) and \(g = 9.8\,\text{m/s}^2\), the time is \(t = 18/9.8 \approx 1.84\,\text{s}\).

parts.stem: Which statement best describes the package's acceleration while it is in flight?

options.text: The acceleration is zero at the top of the path.
options.explanation: The velocity becomes zero at the top, but gravity still acts there. Zero velocity does not imply zero acceleration.

options.text: The acceleration is downward and approximately \(9.8\,\text{m/s}^2\) throughout the flight.
options.explanation: With air resistance neglected, gravity is the only significant force on the package after launch. That means the acceleration remains essentially constant at \(-g\), or downward with magnitude \(9.8\,\text{m/s}^2\), during the entire motion.

options.text: The acceleration points upward while the package rises and downward while it falls.
options.explanation: This confuses the direction of velocity with the direction of acceleration. The package can move upward while its acceleration still points downward.

options.text: The acceleration decreases linearly to zero as the package approaches the top.
options.explanation: Nothing in the idealized model makes gravity weaken near the top of the path. The acceleration does not taper to zero in standard projectile motion.
